rubrics.criterion: After the repair, the task list view and the sorted-tasks view obtain the records they render (the collection contents, its size, and any ordered view) through behavior on the task record store rather than by indexing, size-probing or copying the store's stored collection from the task feature.
rubrics.rationale: These two rendering flows are the case's read-side manifestations; the task prompt explicitly lists them among the flows that still reach into the store.

rubrics.criterion: Changing one task entry - renaming, setting a priority, deleting one task - is resolved inside the task record store: locating the record among the stored records and producing the updated or filtered collection happens store-side, with the feature only supplying which entry and what new value.
rubrics.rationale: The three single-entry mutation flows are the case's update-side manifestations; leaving any of them rebuilding the collection in the feature leaves the pattern the task describes.

rubrics.criterion: Creating a tag no longer constructs the tag record or allocates its identifier in the feature: record construction (including field layout and the id drawn from the tag counter), insertion and counter advancement are performed by the tag record store.
rubrics.rationale: Tag creation is the tag collection's creation lifecycle phase; the tag counter work is one of the clearest pieces of record authority left outside its holder in the case.

rubrics.criterion: The tag removal flow keeps its menu presentation in the feature but the record-side work - sizing the collection, re-indexing it for the numbered menu, and resolving which records survive a removal - is performed by the tag record store, including the remove-everything branch.
rubrics.rationale: Tag teardown is the most touch-heavy manifestation in the case; a menu loop is presentation, but the indexing, survivor resolution and rewrite it currently performs are record work.

rubrics.criterion: Creating a todo entry and creating a reminder entry both leave record construction (message, date and progress fields together with the identifier) and counter advancement to their record store, rather than assembling the record and bumping the shared counter in the two feature flows.
rubrics.rationale: The two creation flows duplicate the same record-authority pattern; fixing one flow but not the other leaves the shared counter managed from outside its owner.

rubrics.criterion: The removal flow shared by todo and reminder collections keeps selection and presentation in the feature while the store side owns consulting the invalid-entry handling, sizing the collection, walking it for cleanup and composing the surviving collection, including the remove-everything branch.
rubrics.rationale: This shared flow is the case's cross-collection teardown phase; it reads a decode-status flag kept on the store and rebuilds the survivors collection from the feature today.

rubrics.criterion: Routine creation and deletion operate through the routine record store's behavior: inserting a named command list (including first-use map initialization), membership-testing and removing a named routine are store-side, with the module functions only passing the request and reporting the outcome.
rubrics.rationale: The two routine module functions are the case's module-level manifestations; keying into and popping out of the store's own mapping from outside is the same relation in mapping form.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair the record-store classes carry real behavior for their collections (operations for creation, lookup or listing, ordering, entry modification, teardown or emptiness), rather than only the load and save plumbing they were extracted with; the specific names and shapes of those operations are free.
rubrics.rationale: Moving the record work to the holders is the point of the change; a repair that relocates no behavior onto the store module would leave the extraction as hollow as before.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not route record access back to direct memory-file or memory-API access from the feature classes: the record stores remain the only addressable persistence point for these collections, and the shared memory file keeps exactly the single writer route it has today.
rubrics.rationale: Bypassing the stores would erase the module the case is built around and reintroduce the repeated persistence ceremony the extraction was meant to remove; the task prompt sets this as a hard compatibility line.

rubrics.criterion: Presentation decisions - prompt wording, menu numbering, colors, and the formatting of entries for display - remain in the feature classes after the repair, and every user-visible string the flows print is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The boundary the task draws is record work versus presentation; a repair that drags interface output into the data holders, or rewrites wording while relocating logic, changes behavior the task declared stable.

rubrics.criterion: The store operations added by the repair perform the record work themselves (constructing records, locating entries, resolving survivors, ordering); the repair does not merely add thin field-forwarding accessors that hand the raw collection or counters back so the features can keep rebuilding and re-keying them from outside.
rubrics.rationale: The case's record work is reconstruction and allocation authority, not field spelling; pass-through get/set shims would leave every decision in the features while only changing syntax.

rubrics.criterion: The tag feature's pre-extraction id-allocation helper and tag-save helper (the jarvis-API versions that the store now replaces for these flows) are removed, or retained only as delegations to the store with no parallel id or save state left, so tag identifiers have exactly one allocation path.
rubrics.rationale: These leftover helpers are obsolete the moment tag creation and teardown go through the store; keeping a second counter path is a concrete cleanup obligation of this case.

rubrics.criterion: The pre-extraction id-allocation helper on the shared todo/reminder base class (which reads its counter through the jarvis API) is likewise removed or reduced to a delegation, so no flow can allocate an id outside the record stores.
rubrics.rationale: With entry creation moved store-side, this older counter helper is dead duplicate bookkeeping for the same shared counter and belongs to the same cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not reintroduce a feature-side save-the-whole-collection helper for the task records in addition to the store's persistence, and does not leave an unused such helper behind: there is exactly one write-back path per collection.
rubrics.rationale: The extraction already retired the task feature's whole-collection rewrite helper; a repair that re-adds one (or keeps one around unused) recreates a second persistence authority for the same records.

rubrics.criterion: The persisted data shapes survive the repair unchanged: the task collection keeps its own memory file with its bare name records; tags remain a plain list of id/name records; todo and reminder collections keep their string envelope; routines keep their name-to-commands mapping; and every key name is untouched.
rubrics.rationale: Re-serializing a collection, renaming its key or merging files would silently destroy existing user data across the CLI's restarts - the exact compatibility line the task sets.

rubrics.criterion: Identifier allocation keeps its observable semantics: todo and reminder entries continue drawing ids from one shared counter across both collections (never restarting per collection, never starting at one), the first allocation still yields 0, and the tag counter keeps its own independent sequence.
rubrics.rationale: The shared todo/reminder counter is original behavior the task explicitly fences; per-collection resets or renumbering would break existing saved entries' identity relationships.

rubrics.criterion: The interactive selection flows still act on the entry the user chooses: menu positions remain one-based, and renaming, prioritizing or deleting the Nth entry still targets that entry (not its neighbor), for tasks, tags and todo/reminder entries alike.
rubrics.rationale: Moving locate-by-position into the store shifts index arithmetic across a boundary; an off-by-one in that move is the most plausible silent breakage of this refactor.

rubrics.criterion: The sorted view behaves exactly as before: name ordering remains ascending, priority ordering remains reversed with its original priority-to-rank treatment (including how unset and undecodable priorities rank), and the odd size short-circuit in front of it keeps its original quirk rather than being reworked.
rubrics.rationale: The ordering strategy moves into the store with this repair, and the pre-existing short-circuit bug is something the task explicitly says must survive - silently fixing it changes flow behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Entries whose dates fail decoding keep being handled exactly as before - the decode-problem state is still tracked per collection, still affects the corresponding removal flow the same way, and no repaired flow crashes on or newly formats such entries.
rubrics.rationale: The decode-error flag follows the store boundary during this repair; dropping or re-scoping it changes which entries the removal flows present and keep.

rubrics.criterion: The remove-everything tags path keeps its current observable outcome, ending the way it ends today after the cleanup it performs, rather than being silently corrected into a clean or crashing-differently path.
rubrics.rationale: This pre-existing quirk is explicitly fenced by the task prompt; a repair that normalizes it changes user-visible behavior the case marked stable.

rubrics.criterion: Removing a tag still triggers the same cross-collection cleanup of the reminder entries that carried it, the same number of times, with the same resulting stored records.
rubrics.rationale: Tag teardown reaches across two collections in this case; a store-side rewrite that drops the reminder cleanup or applies it twice silently corrupts reminders.
